<user_story>
**As a** solo developer installing Fleet as a built artifact rather than running it from a git checkout,
**I want to** have the migration trail ship alongside the compiled daemon,
**so that** the cwd-independence fix holds for the shipped binary and not only for `tsx` in the source tree.
</user_story>

<objective>
Close the packaging half of `01-VERIFICATION.md` gap item (a): "verify `drizzle/` ships alongside the built daemon." Plan 01-05 made the migrations folder resolve relative to the executing module and gave the resolver a packaged-layout candidate (`../drizzle`); nothing yet puts anything at that path, so that candidate is currently unreachable in a real build. This plan makes it real and proves it with the built artifact, then syncs the stale requirements tracker.

Purpose: `tsc` only compiles `.ts` under `rootDir` and never copies non-TS assets — `01-PATTERNS.md` records this as a genuine no-analog gap with no prior art in the repo. Without an explicit copy step the built daemon has no migration trail at all.

Output: a portable asset-copy step in the build script, a constrained `files` field, an out-of-process regression test against the BUILT daemon, and an accurate requirements tracker.
</objective>

  <name>Task 1: Ship the migration trail with the build output</name>

  <files>package.json</files>

  <precondition>Plan 01-05 is merged: `src/db/migrations-path.ts` exists and its first candidate is the one-level-up (packaged) layout. This task's copy destination must match that candidate exactly; if 01-05 shipped a different candidate order, align to what is on disk rather than to this description.</precondition>

  <reversibility rating="reversible">The copy step and `files` field are additive `package.json` entries; removing them restores the previous build behaviour in one edit, and the resolver's checkout-layout candidate keeps a git-checkout run working either way.</reversibility>

  <read_first>
    - `package.json` — current `scripts` block (`build` is `tsc -p tsconfig.json` and nothing else), the `bin` field pointing at `./dist/cli/index.js`, and the absence of any `files` field
    - `tsconfig.json` — `rootDir: src`, `outDir: dist`, `include: ["src/**/*.ts"]`; this is why no non-TS asset ever reaches `dist/`
    - `drizzle.config.ts` — `out: './drizzle'`, the source location of the trail
    - `src/db/migrations-path.ts` — the candidate list created in plan 01-05; the copy destination must be its first (packaged) candidate
    - `.gitignore` — `dist/` is ignored, so build output is safe to produce during tests
    - `.planning/phases/01-foundation-registry-state-machine/01-PATTERNS.md` (packaging note, lines 65-76) — the recorded no-analog gap and the hop-count consistency warning
  </read_first>

  <action>
    Add a `scripts.build:assets` entry to `package.json` that copies the repository-root `drizzle/` directory, including its `meta/` subdirectory, into `dist/drizzle/`. Change `scripts.build` to run the TypeScript compile and then that asset step, so a single `npm run build` produces a complete artifact.

    Use a portable copy. `cp -r` differs between GNU and BSD in ways that bite when the destination already exists from a previous build — a second `npm run build` must produce the same tree as the first, not a nested `dist/drizzle/drizzle/`. Prefer invoking Node's own recursive copy via `node --eval` with `node:fs`'s `cpSync` and `recursive: true` plus `force: true`, which behaves identically on Linux and macOS and is already available with no new dependency. Do not add a dependency for this; do not use a shell builtin or a GNU-only flag. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` fixes the supported platforms at Linux and macOS only — the step does not need to work on Windows, but it does need to work the same on both supported ones.

    Make the step idempotent: running `npm run build` twice in a row must leave `dist/drizzle/meta/_journal.json` at that exact path both times.

    Add a `files` field to `package.json` enumerating exactly what the daemon needs at runtime: the build output directory and the migration trail. Enumerate entries explicitly rather than globbing the repository root — an over-broad `files` field is how planning artifacts, scratch databases, and `.env`-adjacent material get published, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` makes no-`.env`-propagation a stated constraint. Note that `.gitignore` lists `dist/`, which npm's packing rules treat differently from `.npmignore`; the explicit `files` allowlist is what makes the built output ship deterministically regardless.

    Do not touch `dependencies` or `devDependencies` — no new package is needed and adding one would trip the package-legitimacy gate that `<threat_model>` T-01-SC records as not firing for this plan set.

    Do not change `bin`, `main`, or the `test`/`typecheck`/`lint` scripts.
  </action>

  <verify>
    <automated>npm run build && test -f dist/drizzle/meta/_journal.json</automated>
    <automated>npm run build && npm run build && test -f dist/drizzle/meta/_journal.json && test ! -e dist/drizzle/drizzle</automated>
  </verify>

  <acceptance_criteria>
    - After `rm -rf dist && npm run build`, the file `dist/drizzle/meta/_journal.json` exists and its contents are byte-identical to `drizzle/meta/_journal.json`.
    - Every `.sql` file present in `drizzle/` is present in `dist/drizzle/` after a build; compare the two directory listings for equality.
    - Running `npm run build` twice consecutively leaves `dist/drizzle/meta/_journal.json` at that path and creates no nested `dist/drizzle/drizzle` directory.
    - `package.json` has a `files` field whose entries are explicit paths, containing no `*` glob rooted at the repository root and no entry naming `.planning`.
    - `package.json`'s `dependencies` and `devDependencies` blocks are byte-identical to their pre-task contents.
    - `npm run typecheck` exits 0 and `npm test` exits 0 after the change.
  </acceptance_criteria>

  <done>A clean `npm run build` produces a `dist/` that carries its own migration trail at the exact path the resolver's packaged-layout candidate looks for.</done>
</task>

  <behavior>
    - Test 1: after a real `npm run build`, `dist/drizzle/meta/_journal.json` exists.
    - Test 2: `node dist/cli/index.js daemon`, spawned as a real out-of-process child with `cwd` set to a fresh scratch directory that is not the Fleet repo root, `FLEET_HOME` set to a fresh temp directory, and `FLEET_PORT` set to a reserved free port, becomes ready and answers `GET /health` with 200. This is the first test in the suite to exercise the resolver's packaged-layout candidate.
    - Test 3: that same built daemon serves `GET /projects` with 200 and an empty array against its fresh `FLEET_HOME` — proving migrations actually ran against the new database file rather than the daemon merely binding a port (the STATE-01 empty edge, from the built artifact).
    - Test 4: the migration trail copied into the build output preserves the journal's recorded entry order exactly as it appears in the source `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` (the STATE-01 ordering edge).
  </behavior>

  <action>
    Create `src/db/packaging.e2e.test.ts` in the `unit` vitest project — a plain `.test.ts`, not `.spike.test.ts`, since it spawns Fleet's own build output and never the real `claude` CLI.

    Implement `buildOnce()` as a `beforeAll` that runs `npm run build` exactly once for the file, capturing stdout and stderr and failing the suite with them attached on a non-zero exit. Give the hook an explicit generous timeout — a `tsc` compile of this project plus the asset copy takes several seconds, well beyond vitest's default hook timeout. Building once per file, not once per test, keeps the cost bounded. The root-level `fileParallelism: false` in `vitest.config.ts` means no other test file runs while this one mutates `dist/`.

    Implement `startBuiltDaemonChild()` by spawning `process.execPath` with the resolved absolute path to `dist/cli/index.js` and the `daemon` argument — deliberately NOT through `tsx`, because the entire point is to exercise the compiled artifact's own module location. Pass an explicit `cwd` (a `mkdtemp` scratch directory), and `env` extending the current environment with `FLEET_HOME` and `FLEET_PORT`. Accumulate stdout and stderr so a readiness timeout reports the child's actual startup error rather than a bare timeout.

    Reuse the readiness-polling and free-port shapes introduced in `src/registry/cwd-independence.e2e.test.ts`. If those helpers are not exported from that file, duplicate them locally rather than exporting test internals across test files — a small duplication is preferable to coupling two regression suites whose failure modes must stay independently legible.

    This test must not skip. It must not tolerate a missing `dist/`, a build failure, or a readiness timeout by passing — every one of those conditions is the packaging gap itself and must be red. Prohibition P-03 (authored in `01-05-PLAN.md`) applies directly: a conditionally-skipped packaging test would recreate the exact blind spot this gap-closure set exists to close.

    Kill the daemon child and remove every temp directory in `afterEach`/`afterAll`, following `scratch-repo.ts`'s cleanup guarantee. A leaked built-daemon child holds its port and would poison subsequent runs.

    For Test 4, read both `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` and `dist/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, parse each, and compare the recorded entry sequence for equality — assert on the ordered sequence, not on set membership or entry count, since a re-sorted trail would pass a count check while applying migrations in the wrong order.
  </action>

  <verify>
    <automated>npx vitest run --project unit src/db/packaging.e2e.test.ts</automated>
    <automated>npm test</automated>
  </verify>

  <acceptance_criteria>
    - `npx vitest run --project unit src/db/packaging.e2e.test.ts` exits 0 with all four tests passing.
    - Removing the asset-copy step from `scripts.build` makes Tests 1, 2, 3, and 4 fail. Confirm by temporary local revert before committing — this is the criterion that proves the test covers the packaging gap rather than incidentally passing off a stale `dist/`.
    - The daemon child in Test 2 is spawned with `dist/cli/index.js` in its argv and no reference to `tsx`.
    - The daemon child's `cwd` option is a `mkdtemp` scratch directory and is not the repository root.
    - The file contains no `.skip`, no `.todo`, no conditional `return` that would bypass an assertion, and no try/catch that swallows a failed readiness poll.
    - Test 3 asserts on the `GET /projects` response body being an empty array, not merely on the status code — a 200 alone does not prove migrations ran.
    - Test 4 compares the journal entry sequences in order.
    - `npm test` exits 0 for the whole `unit` project.
  </acceptance_criteria>

  <done>The compiled daemon, running from a directory it has never seen, finds its own migration trail, migrates a fresh database, and serves — proven by a test that is red without the build's asset step.</done>
